IMG_4359_2.title: Seventy-Five of These
IMG_4359_2.summary: Late-night hardware count at the workshop: 'We don't need them, bring them back — there's only 75 of these in there.' The armory begins as a pile of small parts.

IMG_4417_2.title: We Almost Built a Fire
IMG_4417_2.summary: Arrival at the Tool Maker's shop: Yovel and the crew tried cutting this wood with a grinder and it started smoking. Time for the expert cut.

IMG_4418_2.title: Cut Right on the Line
IMG_4418_2.summary: The Tool Maker teaches: set the saw, keep it true — 'when you put it on there, it's going to cut right on the line.' A master class in nineteen seconds.

IMG_4423_2.title: Take a Little Off
IMG_4423_2.summary: Seven seconds of shop judgment: 'I think we gotta off this a little bit.' Measure twice, trim once.

IMG_4428_2.title: Don't Touch It With Your Hands
IMG_4428_2.summary: Blade check between cuts — 'Let's see the blade… don't touch it with your hands. It might be alright, let's try it.' Shop safety, learned live.

IMG_4429_2.title: Metal Saw Horses
IMG_4429_2.summary: The blade meets the sawhorse: 'So it was kind of my fault but not exactly — we got to watch that these are metal saw horses.' A lesson kept on tape.

IMG_4430_2.title: Between Cuts
IMG_4430_2.summary: Saw noise and shop air — the whisper heard nothing worth words. The work does the talking.

IMG_4431_2.title: Oh
IMG_4431_2.summary: Two seconds, one syllable: 'Oh.' A reaction shot from the cutting session.

IMG_4432_2.title: Cut That Podcast Now
IMG_4432_2.summary: 'Don't wait for inspiration — cut that podcast now.' … 'He's the Tool Maker.' Shop philosophy, delivered between cuts.

IMG_4433_2.title: Wish We'd Cleaned Up Ours
IMG_4433_2.summary: Craftsmanship honesty, comparing their cut to the Tool Maker's: 'We kind of did a bad — wish we clean up the one that we did.'

IMG_4434_2.title: Pretty, But Not Tool Maker Smooth
IMG_4434_2.summary: 'It's definitely pretty, but not nearly as smooth as the Tool Maker['s].' The standard has been set.

IMG_4435_2.title: Make It a Good One
IMG_4435_2.summary: A minute of cutting-floor chatter — 'I'm gonna make it a good one again' — pull it, move it back, clear the end. Persistence, mostly wordless.

IMG_4439_2.title: 2:35 AM at the Tool Maker's
IMG_4439_2.summary: The session's last clip, timestamped deep in the night; no words captured. The shop goes quiet.

2026-04-22-shaka-jade.title: A Month of Labor for a Ticket
2026-04-22-shaka-jade.summary: Shaka (from 4Seas, Chiang Mai) and Jade meet for the first time: a month of build-week labor, music, and teardown offered as a gift for a ticket, food, and a place to sleep.
2026-04-22-shaka-jade.digest: Shaka, calling from Chiang Mai, pitches Jade a burn-veteran's bargain: a full month of build-week labor, instruments, and Open Source Orchestra energy — a gift, not a fee — for a ticket and camp care [13:17]. His credibility is three years of burns, including saving a flying dome cover in a whiteout [16:18], and the veteran's caution that 'the playa usually tends to humble you' [15:41]. Adds up to: the camp may have landed its build-week workhorse and music lead, pending Jeremy's sign-off.

2026-05-12-tarobot-intro.title: Hiring a Robot Fortune Teller
2026-05-12-tarobot-intro.summary: Jeremy and Jade pitch roboticist Daniel Ritchie on the camp's AI oracle tents; he demos his talking robot and delivers the key advice: don't trust Starlink — run local compute.
2026-05-12-tarobot-intro.digest: The oracle tent goes from robot-shopping to a real plan. Daniel demos his full-motion conversational robot, prices always-on AI at roughly $100/hour, then makes the pivotal call: playa connectivity will fail, so steer toward a local server running open-source models [06:58]. The concept stated plainly — AI-driven oracle tents as the camp's offering [00:27] — and Daniel warming to coming along as 'a tech roadie kind of thing' [18:20]. Adds up to: local-first AI, a possible robot collab, and a May 30 preview party.

2026-05-14-kitchen-trailer.title: Boil-in-Bag Dinners and a Piggyback Deal
2026-05-14-kitchen-trailer.summary: Food expert James Tramel teaches his 250-person camp's system — premade boil-in-bag meals, one stock pot, almost no dishwashing — and lets the turtles piggyback on his July order.
2026-05-14-kitchen-trailer.digest: James's camp abandoned scratch cooking for half-gallon boil-in-bag meals: one bag is five servings, shelf-stable 60 days, heated in boiling water [09:38]. He agrees to let the first-year camp piggyback on his order with on-playa pickup — what David calls 'the biggest gift here' [46:16]. Skip the $8k thermalizing oven; one big stock pot does the whole meal. Adds up to: a realistic low-labor dinner plan, plus the warning that matters most — 'not infrastructure, it's members' [01:00:31].

2026-05-15-laurence.title: Drawing Borders Over a Water Bladder
2026-05-15-laurence.summary: With side-by-side placement confirmed, the turtles and Laurence Ion's longevity camp negotiate what neighbors share: water yes, food no, showers separate — kitchens adjacent.
2026-05-15-laurence.digest: Neighbor diplomacy, playa style. Laurence proposes the two camps jointly buy a water bladder and share pumps and hoses [09:52]; food is explicitly off the table — 'I'm not open to sharing food because we have healthy food' [16:59] — and each camp builds its own shower. The surprise consequence: share water and the kitchen trailer should park next to his kitchen [17:40]. Adds up to: a friendly framework with every real decision waiting on actual maps.

2026-05-21-david-food.title: Four Suppliers and the Influencer Warning
2026-05-21-david-food.summary: David turns the food piggyback into a four-supplier system, sets hard deadlines, and delivers a culture warning: never let the word 'influencer' leave your lips at Burning Man.
2026-05-21-david-food.digest: The camp shifts from loosey-goosey to nuts-and-bolts. David lays out the whole food strategy in one line — 'your four suppliers will be Costco, Chef Store, Bonanza and the premade meals' [14:44] — and debunks kitchen myths (eggs survive the burn unrefrigerated). The sharpest beat is cultural: 'You should never let the word influencer leave your lips' [21:18]. Adds up to: hard deadlines, a menu due in three weeks, and the real gap named — warm bodies [08:47].

2026-06-03-tarobot-daniel.title: Blank Canvas Robots, Council of Oracles
2026-06-03-tarobot-daniel.summary: At Daniel Ritchie's Denver demo space the oracle tents get their embodiment: cheap open-source desktop robots, hot-swappable backups, a 24/7 single-robot MVP, a stretch 'council of robots'.
2026-06-03-tarobot-daniel.digest: Daniel demos a blank-canvas robot — eye-tracking, emotion-lit eyes, beamforming mics — and Jeremy commits to resilience over dazzle: one 24/7 single-robot oracle tent that survives total infrastructure failure [12:11]. Daniel's redundancy canon: 'backup robots that are just sitting in a box… unplug it, plug in the backup and you're immediately running' [28:59]. Adds up to: two proposals and a quality bar — the oracle must not feel like 'a random number generator' [57:27]. Speaker tags are all wrong in this file; quotes unattributable by tag.

2026-06-07-david-planning.title: You've Had the Signal for Three Months
2026-06-07-david-planning.summary: David's message: stop waiting on me — the shade parts were cleared to order months ago. He sets a weekly rhythm and specs the camp: power drops, IBC totes, fridges, stoves, tents.
2026-06-07-david-planning.digest: The mentor draws the line: 'you've had the signal for me for three months' [13:29] — the blocker is the camp's own hesitation, and his available time is evaporating [07:41]. Around that spine he specs everything: two 70-amp drops, 10-gauge cords, food-safe IBC totes (beware the ones that held whiskey [33:41]), renter fridges, Backyard Pro stoves, trifold mattresses. Adds up to: an ordering green light, shared human-made documents, and homework before next week's call.

2026-06-11-cold-yogis-a.title: Neighbor Camps Trade Playa Wisdom
2026-06-11-cold-yogis-a.summary: The turtles meet their neighbors, the Cold Yogis. Veteran Dustin converts every problem into an easy button: porta-potties, leapfrogging gray-water totes, maybe shared metered water.
2026-06-11-cold-yogis-a.digest: Dustin, the playa veteran, hands over the survival playbook: skip pricey eco-toilets for locked porta-potties, and run two gray-water totes in leapfrog — fill one, pump the other [08:22] — because one full tote means your water supply is off. The biggest offer: shared metered fresh-water infrastructure, cost-split between camps [13:20]. Adds up to: a playbook, two open offers to mull, and a neighbor relationship sealed with 'you will survive' [02:30]. (Twin file -b is the same call with a different header time.)

2026-06-19-coordination-1a.title: State of the Union, Camp Agent
2026-06-19-coordination-1a.summary: First internal coordination call: the camp map squeeze, one human per domain, and Shaka's signature idea — a giant runbook powering a camp agent that knows where every hammer is.
2026-06-19-coordination-1a.digest: The camp's first full state of the union. The oversized shade forces building from the Cold Yogis border toward Fountain of Youth; meanwhile Jeremy's one-human-per-domain plan fuses with Shaka's proposal to 'build out our camp agent that just, like, knows everything' [26:08] — because without it, 'we could either end up with a hundred hammers, or everybody thought it was their hammer' [31:07]. Adds up to: every domain scoped, and an AI runbook committed as 'a really cool gift to give to the playa' [46:58].

2026-06-26-coordination-2.title: This Could Be Our Shower
2026-06-26-coordination-2.summary: Second coordination call: the shower breakthrough (two used IBC totes plus a propane camping hot-water unit), a hard shipping timeline, and menu math still unfinished.
2026-06-26-coordination-2.digest: The shower design is born live on the call: 'buying two used IBC totes, cutting the tops off, putting them together' with a propane instant-hot-water camping unit [18:16] — 'I think this is. This could be our shower' [29:04]. Around it the deadline cascade locks in: parts ordered by Aug 1, kitchen trailer packed by ~Aug 10, driven out Aug 13–15. Adds up to: a concrete water strategy and a ship date, with the menu still unwritten. (And yes, someone asks the AI to buy a crate of tampons [04:11].)

2026-06-26-david-shade-kitchen.title: Talk About It, Then Execute
2026-06-26-david-shade-kitchen.summary: David imposes drop-dead dates and purchasing discipline: 'We no longer have time to talk about anything ever over again. You have to talk about it. And then execute.'
2026-06-26-david-shade-kitchen.digest: The mentor converts goodwill into an execution machine — his rate rises to $400/hr July 1 and $500/hr Aug 1, and the thesis is blunt: 'we no longer have time to talk about anything ever over again' [24:02] — talk about it, then execute. The dates stack: trailer ~Aug 1, kitchen ready ~Aug 10, Yovel departs Aug 19, Reno Aug 21, gates Aug 24. Power is billed by peak amps, notebook in hand [46:38], and the Veggie Coffin gets its first full spec — 4x8x3, a lid, an AC at each end [31:32]. Adds up to: a weekly-meeting machine where slipping a week triggers alarm.

2026-07-02-david-sync.title: Float Switches Are Magic
2026-07-02-david-sync.summary: The definitive shower download: two IBC totes per pod, no mortar tub, a riser in the bottom tote, float switches pumping to dryness — containment is the hardest part.
2026-07-02-david-sync.digest: Six weeks out, David walks the master spreadsheet line by line. The shower pod hinges entirely on gray-water containment: skip the mortar tub, stand on a riser inside the bottom IBC, and 'get these float switches in your hands because they are magic' [01:30:51] — 'how you do the containment on a shower is the hardest part of the whole project' [01:34:42]. Adds up to: a verified order list, a working water flow (IBC to pump to valved splitter), a 70-amp power budget to fill in, and David's allocation ethics [01:25:29].

2026-07-09-david-sync.title: Taps, Troughs, and a Thousand Miles
2026-07-09-david-sync.summary: The gap is knowledge, not supplies: David explains what a tap even is before assigning keder-rail homework, Shaka pledges a musician's labor, the truck needs practice miles.
2026-07-09-david-sync.digest: Parts are arriving; now they must become assemblies. David teaches tapping from zero so Yuval can hang 64 ft of keder rail 12 ft up the semi — the click moment: 'you are attaching the keter rail to the side of the semi trailer' [25:20]. Shaka disarms the tension: 'I'm playing music for the Ethereum conference this year. I'm not a mechanic, but I'm gonna work my ass off' [32:47]. The delivery-driver drama ('extorted me for money' [01:32:33]) stays unresolved. Adds up to: watch the videos, pick up foam and totes, build.

2026-07-16-david-sync.title: The Machine Meets the Mentor
2026-07-16-david-sync.summary: Jarrett 'The Machine' Henson's first David sync: pump, power, keder rail, and float-switch downloads — and an instant mind-meld: 'I like how your brain works.'
2026-07-16-david-sync.digest: The team felt lost because parts were gathered but never explained — so David delivers 'downloads' all meeting: braided hoses stay on the pump forever, 70-amp feeds terminate in mobile duplex panels, keder rail is cut to land on supports. Jarrett Henson, introduced as new build muscle [06:30], asks the master-electrician's-kid questions [27:57] until David lands it: 'the picture that's in your head is the one that's in my head… I'm going to lean on you a lot' [40:31]. Jarrett's answer: 100% of infrastructure done by end of next week [43:03]. Adds up to: the camp found its Machine.

2026-07-16-david-sync-JADE-NOTES.digest: The same 7/16 download session, rendered as a ledger. Jade captures the meta-lesson: the team felt lost because parts arrived without assembly knowledge — David's 'downloads' are the missing manual. Every promise gets an owner: Jarrett owes keder cutting and stake welding, Jeremy owes float-switch weights and the RV balance, Jade owes the map fix and the master-list share, David owes the hydraulic shop name. Adds up to: the week the camp's homework became trackable. (Notes file — no timestamps to anchor.)

pit_digest: A village gets built. In the meetings, the mind: David's downloads turn gathered parts into systems — water, power, shade, cold chain — and The Machine arrives to accelerate. In the footage, the hands: the Tool Maker's clean cuts, the coffin glued and screwed, the trailer machinified, and finally the shower running. Between them, the armory: 277 items, each a decision made visible. Move slow, bite things.

machine_guidance.canon_quote: Just as the Admiral is a machine guiding me, Jarred is the Machine guiding our build.
machine_guidance.opener: Every camp gets one: the human who shows up, and the machines start listening. Jarred 'The Machine' Henson — welding, keder rails, electrical — walked into Phoenix Gulch, and the build caught up with its dreams.

clips.one_liner: THE SHOWER RUNS — water flowing at last, and the naming itself: 'you just bring in the experts like Jared the machine.' Nineteen seconds of pure victory.
THE TRAILER, MACHINIFIED — the electrical walkthrough: transfer switch (panel/battery, generator kill), 16 outlets, 30A both sides, USB/USB-C. 'The machine turned the trailer into a machine.'

THE WATER LOOP, END TO END — a complete lesson from IBC coupler to greywater tank: thread tape, channel locks, cam-lock, transfer pump, foot switch, float switches, sump. 'Really appreciate you, machine!'
